findings.trigger: Any request to /embed/best where TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed returns a topic_id, causing the 'best' template to render

validated_findings.body: The template compiles to `end if` followed by a separator, which is a Ruby SyntaxError (or, at best, silently reorders buffer appends via modifier-if parsing), so the embed comments view 500s or renders incorrectly for every existing embedded topic
validated_findings.failure_mode: Template compilation raises SyntaxError at render time, breaking the primary happy path of the embed feature
validated_findings.impact: The template compiles to `end if` followed by a separator, which is a Ruby SyntaxError (or, at best, silently reorders buffer appends via modifier-if parsing), so the embed comments view 500s or renders incorrectly for every existing embedded topic
validated_findings.root_cause: Typo in the ERB block terminator introduces a stray `if` modifier keyword after `end`
validated_findings.title: Invalid ERB block terminator `<%- end if %>` in embed best template
validated_findings.trigger: Any request to /embed/best where TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed returns a topic_id, causing the 'best' template to render
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 6 verbatim shows `<%- end if %>` which is invalid ERB syntax - `end if` is not valid Ruby block termination. This will cause a SyntaxError when the template is compiled/rendered.

validated_findings.body: `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError inside the item loop; the hourly job (retry: false) aborts and no feed items are ever imported for such feeds
validated_findings.failure_mode: Unhandled NoMethodError aborts the entire feed-polling job on the first content-less item
validated_findings.impact: `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError inside the item loop; the hourly job (retry: false) aborts and no feed items are ever imported for such feeds
validated_findings.root_cause: The code assumes every feed item has a `content` field, which only holds for Atom/content:encoded feeds
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Fall back to the description field, e.g. `content = CGI.unescapeHTML((i.content || i.description).to_s.scrub)` and skip items with no body
validated_findings.title: PollFeed crashes on feed items without a <content> element
validated_findings.trigger: Polling a standard RSS 2.0 feed whose items expose only <description> (SimpleRSS returns nil for i.content), which is common for non-Atom feeds
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 35 shows `i.content.scrub` - SimpleRSS returns nil for content on RSS 2.0 feeds that only have description elements. Calling .scrub on nil raises NoMethodError.

validated_findings.body: Kernel#open executes shell commands for '|...' values and reads arbitrary local files for path values, escalating settings-write access to code execution / file disclosure on the server
validated_findings.failure_mode: Setting value is interpreted as a pipe or filesystem path rather than strictly as a URL
validated_findings.impact: Kernel#open executes shell commands for '|...' values and reads arbitrary local files for path values, escalating settings-write access to code execution / file disclosure on the server
validated_findings.root_cause: Kernel#open is used on a configurable string instead of an HTTP-only fetch
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use `URI.parse(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url).open` (or open-uri via an explicit URI object / HTTP client) after validating the scheme is http(s)
validated_findings.title: Kernel#open on admin-supplied feed_polling_url enables command execution and local file reads
validated_findings.trigger: An admin (or anyone able to write the site setting) sets feed_polling_url to a value beginning with '|command' or a local file path; the hourly job then calls Kernel#open on it
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 29 shows `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` using Kernel#open which accepts pipe commands and file paths. Admin-controlled setting could enable command execution via `|command` prefix.

validated_findings.body: Unsanitized third-party HTML is persisted as `cooked` and rendered via `raw post.cooked`, producing stored XSS in the forum and in every embedding page
validated_findings.failure_mode: Externally sourced markup reaches the browser unfiltered
validated_findings.impact: Unsanitized third-party HTML is persisted as `cooked` and rendered via `raw post.cooked`, producing stored XSS in the forum and in every embedding page
validated_findings.root_cause: The new raw_html branch bypasses the entire cooking/sanitization pipeline while PollFeed feeds it externally controlled HTML
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Run raw_html posts through the HTML sanitizer/tag whitelist (as import_remote does via Readability) before storing, instead of returning raw verbatim
validated_findings.title: raw_html cook method stores and renders feed HTML with no sanitization
validated_findings.trigger: PollFeed imports an item whose unescaped content contains <script> or event-handler markup (compromised or malicious feed); the post is created with cook_method raw_html and cooked == raw
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The raw_html cook method is intentional design for RSS imports. The claim assumes PollFeed uses raw_html but examining poll_feed.rb shows it calls TopicEmbed.import which may sanitize content. Without evidence that unsanitized HTML reaches raw_html posts, this is speculative.

validated_findings.body: `start_with?('/')` matches '//' and `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes, rewriting the URL to 'http://sourcehost/cdn.example.com/x.png' — a broken link/image in the imported post
validated_findings.failure_mode: Valid absolute (protocol-relative) URLs are rewritten into nonexistent paths on the source host
validated_findings.impact: `start_with?('/')` matches '//' and `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes, rewriting the URL to 'http://sourcehost/cdn.example.com/x.png' — a broken link/image in the imported post
validated_findings.root_cause: Root-relative detection does not distinguish '/path' from '//host/path'
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Exclude protocol-relative URLs, e.g. `href.start_with?('/') && !href.start_with?('//')` in both the anchor and img loops
validated_findings.title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs (//host/path)
validated_findings.trigger: Imported content contains protocol-relative links or images such as href="//cdn.example.com/x.png"
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 64-65 show `href.start_with?('/')` followed by `href.sub(/^\/+/, '')`. Protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com` match start_with?('/') and get both slashes stripped, corrupting the URL.

validated_findings.body: `force: true` silently drops the existing top_topics table and all its rows before recreating it, causing unannounced data loss; editing a committed migration also breaks migration-history determinism
validated_findings.failure_mode: Silent DROP TABLE on environments that still run or re-run this migration
validated_findings.impact: `force: true` silently drops the existing top_topics table and all its rows before recreating it, causing unannounced data loss; editing a committed migration also breaks migration-history determinism
validated_findings.root_cause: A previously merged migration was modified to destructively drop the table it creates
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Revert this edit to the existing migration; if a drop-and-recreate is genuinely needed, ship it as a new migration without `force: true` data loss
validated_findings.title: force: true added to already-shipped CreateTopTopics migration
validated_findings.trigger: Any environment where this migration executes while a top_topics table already exists (re-run after rollback, restored database, or divergent schema)
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch shows modification of existing migration adding `force: true`. The diff confirms this was changed from `create_table :top_topics do` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do`. Modifying shipped migrations with force:true risks data loss.

validated_findings.body: The iframe requests 'http://forum.example.comembed/best?...', a nonexistent host/path, so the embed silently never loads
validated_findings.failure_mode: Malformed iframe URL when the configured base lacks a trailing slash
validated_findings.impact: The iframe requests 'http://forum.example.comembed/best?...', a nonexistent host/path, so the embed silently never loads
validated_findings.root_cause: Naive string concatenation of a user-configured base URL and a path with no normalization
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Normalize the base, e.g. append '/' when `discourseUrl` does not end with one, before concatenating the path
validated_findings.title: iframe src concatenation assumes discourseUrl ends with a trailing slash
validated_findings.trigger: A site owner defines discourseUrl = 'http://forum.example.com' (no trailing slash), which nothing in this script validates or documents
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 7 shows string concatenation `discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."` without ensuring trailing slash. If discourseUrl lacks trailing slash, URL becomes malformed.

validated_findings.body: Messages from non-Discourse origins pass the check and can manipulate the embed iframe (e.g. force arbitrary heights), weakening the intended origin restriction
validated_findings.failure_mode: Origin validation accepts unintended sender origins
validated_findings.impact: Messages from non-Discourse origins pass the check and can manipulate the embed iframe (e.g. force arbitrary heights), weakening the intended origin restriction
validated_findings.root_cause: indexOf substring containment used as an origin equality check
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Compare the message origin exactly against the origin parsed from discourseUrl (e.g. `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin + '/') !== 0` guard or exact origin equality)
validated_findings.title: postMessage origin check uses substring match instead of exact origin comparison
validated_findings.trigger: A message posted from any window whose origin is a substring/prefix of discourseUrl (e.g. an attacker-registered 'http://forum.example.co' when discourseUrl is 'http://forum.example.com/')
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 17 shows `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` which is substring containment, not exact origin match. An attacker origin that is substring of discourseUrl would pass this check.

validated_findings.body: The specs pass even if the url/username guards are deleted from PollFeed#execute, so they do not verify the behavior their names claim
validated_findings.failure_mode: Vacuously green tests provide false coverage of the guard conditions
validated_findings.impact: The specs pass even if the url/username guards are deleted from PollFeed#execute, so they do not verify the behavior their names claim
validated_findings.root_cause: Tests rely on the guarded setting alone while an earlier condition in the && chain already fails by default
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Stub `SiteSetting.stubs(:feed_polling_enabled?).returns(true)` (and the other prerequisite settings) in these two examples so only the setting under test is missing
validated_findings.title: PollFeed setting-requirement specs pass vacuously without stubbing feed_polling_enabled?
validated_findings.trigger: Running the 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' examples: feed_polling_enabled? defaults to false in test, so execute short-circuits before ever evaluating the stubbed setting
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 18-21 show test stubs feed_polling_url to nil but doesn't stub feed_polling_enabled? to true. Since execute() checks feed_polling_enabled? first in the && chain, the test passes vacuously without testing the url guard.
